newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares gain on back of higher bonds.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares gain on back of higher bonds.

text.p: Israeli shares rose for the fourth consecutive session on high turnover following another rise in bond prices, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.38 points, or 0.73 percent, to 190.19 on an high all-share turnover of 101.5 million shekels against 75 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 index rose 0.59 percent to 199.57.

"Once again the bond market was pushing the stock market. The identity of the buyers in the bond market is a real mystery. There are rumours that foreign investors started buying bonds but nobody knows if it's true," said Izik Winish at Capital Securities.

"The positive trend in the stock market will only continue if the bond market keeps rising. But the rise in bond prices depends on the mysterious investors and it's very difficult to predict what will happen in the near future," Winish added.

Koor Industries, the most active share, rose 2.0 percent to 27,542 on high volume of 9.3 million shekels. Koor announced it will join Makhteshim Chemical Works and Agan Chemical Manufacturers under one new holding company. Shareholders in the two companies will be offered the chance to exchange their shares for those in a new holding company, M.A.G.M. Chemistry Holdings.

"This is a logical step as there is significant synergy between the two companies and the cost of savings in production and domestic sales should be significant. The first impression is that this must be good for existing shareholders of both entities," said a Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull Securities analyst.
Makhteshim rose 2.5 percent to 1,897 and Agan gained 3.0 percent to 5,286.
"The mood in the market has changed completely and activity is rising. In the next few days we might see some profit taking but the general trend is positive," said a trader at Lehava Investments.
"This is the first time in the last few months that the trading volume is above 100 million shekels and this is a very good sign," he said.

Other active shares include Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 1.5 percent to 774 on turnover of 4.9 million shekels and IDB Holdings, which gained 2.5 percent to 1,214 on volume of 4.5 million shekels.
